title: Model registry: store tiered batching defaults by model family/variant (versioned + auditable)
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
Goal
Persist tiered batching defaults (fast / standard / cost_efficient) in the model registry in a way that is:
- versioned (so we can roll forward/back with full traceability)
- auditable (who changed what, when, and why)
- parameterized (by model family + variant, and optionally GPU SKU / context-length class)
- rollout-friendly (canary enablement + safe rollback)

Context
Runtime is adding tier selection + workload-aware mapping. We need a single source of truth for tier “base defaults” per model family/variant so:
- Hosted/Dedicated/Private are consistent
- we can patch/tune defaults for a family without redeploying a new runtime build everywhere
- Console can explain “effective config” and show provenance

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Designing the scheduler mapping itself (ENG-18421)
- Building the Console UI (ENG-18425) or explain endpoint (ENG-18470), beyond ensuring we can serve the needed metadata

Requirements
1) Data model
- Store tier defaults at the following minimum granularity:
  - model_family (e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen)
  - model_variant (e.g., 8B, 70B, instruct vs base, long-context variants)
- Optional override dimension(s) supported from day 1:
  - gpu_sku (e.g., H100-80GB, A100-80GB, L40S)
  - context_class (standard vs long-context) OR max_context_bucket (e.g., <=8k, <=32k)
- Each record must include:
  - tier name
  - parameter map (the “knobs” controlled by tier defaults; runtime may derive additional internal params)
  - schema version
  - created_at, created_by, change_reason
  - status: active | deprecated | disabled
  - compatibility constraints (min runtime version, if needed)

2) Versioning semantics
- Immutable versions: updates create a new version; do not mutate in-place.
- Support “pinning” by:
  - exact version (for debugging / regressions)
  - latest active (default behavior)
- Provide a clean rollback path:
  - mark previous version as “active” again
  - or set “disabled” for a tier default to fall back to runtime hardcoded baseline

3) Auditability
- Every change to tier defaults must emit:
  - audit log entry (actor, timestamp, diff summary)
  - pointer to ticket/PR (Linear key + Git SHA) and optional benchmark artifact link
- Minimum required fields in change request:
  - change_reason
  - reviewer (human approval) for production environments

4) API surface
- Read path needed by runtime/config service:
  - GET /model-defaults/{model_id}/batching-tiers (or equivalent internal RPC)
  - must return tier defaults + provenance metadata (version, updated_by, updated_at)
- Write path restricted to internal admins / CI:
  - POST new version
  - PATCH status (active/deprecated/disabled)

5) Precedence rules (align with design spec)
- Runtime behavior precedence:
  1) explicit customer config overrides (ENG-18420)
  2) tier selection (customer-provided) + registry tier defaults
  3) runtime compiled-in baseline defaults (if registry entry missing/disabled)
- Registry precedence within itself:
  - most specific match wins (model+variant+gpu_sku > model+variant > model_family)

6) Migration plan
- Seed initial entries for beta:
  - top 3–5 models by traffic, for H100 + A100
  - include at least one long-context model family/variant
- Provide a one-time backfill script + verification query:
  - confirm every beta model has entries for all tiers

Acceptance criteria
- Registry supports versioned records for tier defaults with immutable history.
- Runtime/config service can retrieve defaults deterministically given (model_id, gpu_sku, tier).
- Audit events exist for create/update/activate/deprecate operations and include Linear key + git sha.
- Backfill script produces entries for the beta model set and passes validation.
- Unit tests for:
  - specificity matching
  - pinning by version
  - disabled fallback
  - schema validation (reject unknown knobs)

Open questions
- Do we represent “knobs” as a strict allowlist (preferred) vs opaque blob? Strong preference: allowlist to prevent accidental no-op parameters.
- Where do we store the ‘min_runtime_version’ guardrail vs leaving that to rollout tooling (ENG-18515)?

Links
- Confluence PRD: workload-aware batching defaults
- ADR-041: SLO-tiered batching profiles
- Related PRs (expected): redwood-model-registry/pr_147

Rollout / risk notes
- Incorrect registry values can cause tail-latency regressions. Require a manual reviewer for activating a new version in prod.
- If registry is unavailable, runtime must gracefully fall back to compiled-in defaults (no hard dependency for serving availability).
comments: [2025-02-10] (Lena Fischer) Starting point: we need to be able to tune tier defaults per model family without waiting on runtime-1.21 rollout everywhere. Ethan—can you own the registry representation + read API? I’ll sync with Sofia on which knobs are “registry-controlled” vs derived.

[2025-02-12] (Ethan Park) Drafted data model proposal: (model_family, variant, gpu_sku?, tier, version) -> params + metadata. Planning strict allowlist for params to avoid silent failures. Will post schema to architecture thread for review.

[2025-02-14] (Sean Gallagher) From SRE side: please include ‘activated_by/activated_at’ separate from created_* so we can track when a version actually hit prod. Also want a status field we can alert on if defaults are missing for a prod model.

[2025-02-18] (Sofia Ivanova) Confirmed knobs we want to store initially: max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill_weight, decode_weight, kv_cache_pressure_limit. Anything else should remain runtime-derived for now.

[2025-02-21] (Ethan Park) Implementing matching precedence: model+variant+gpu_sku > model+variant > family. Adding a ‘context_bucket’ field is doable but might complicate v1; proposing we handle long-context as separate variant naming first (e.g., llama3-8b-32k).

[2025-02-26] (Benji Okafor) Please ensure changes produce audit events compatible with existing rollout tooling. If you can emit a stable ‘config_namespace=batching_tier_defaults’ it’ll plug into ENG-18515 without extra work.

[2025-03-03] (Ethan Park) Backfill script drafted for beta set (llama3-8b-instruct, llama3-70b-instruct, mistral-large, qwen2.5-32b, longctx candidate tbd). Waiting on Aditya to confirm the beta model list + regions.

[2025-03-06] (Ethan Park) PR up in redwood-model-registry (pr_147): adds versioned table + read API; write API gated behind internal role. Still missing: activation workflow + separate activated_* fields per Sean’s request. Targeting updates by end of week.
